Senator Smith Of Oregon Lies (Badly) To A Constituent
To Justify Arresting The Sick And Dying

March 24, 1998

(Ed. note: Senator Gordon H. Smith (R. Oregon) sent the following letter to a constituent who wrote to him about medical marijuana. The Senator’s response was both semi-literate and completely dishonest. If I were a constituent of his, I would be very offended by this. While the editors of the Oregonian might enjoy be lied to about medical marijuana, [See

How The Oregonian Cribs Its Editorials from DEA Handouts] there was absolutely no reason for him to insult this person’s intelligence.)

March 5, 1998

Dear Ms. ……

Thank you for sharing your thoughts regarding the legalization of marijuana and other illegal drugs. I found your comments informative and welcome this opportunity to respond to your concerns.

I strongly oppose any effort to legalize marijuana, or any other illegal drug. I am greatly concerned that marijuana one of the most commonly abused drugs by our actions teenagers. (sic) In fact, according to the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA), marijuana is used by average of ten million Americans each month. Of our nation’s 8th grade students, 15.8 percent use marijuana. I believe that any effort to legalize marijuana or any other illegal drug would only exacerbate this problem and increase the drug-related violent crimes in our state. (Ed. note: What is the relationship between marijuana use and "drug-related violent crimes" in Oregon?)

In recent years, there has been growing support for legalizing the use of marijuana for medicinal purposes nationwide. For patients suffering from terminal illnesses such as AIDS or cancer, marijuana is used legally in some states, including California, to relieve the side effects of chemotherapy and other painful treatments.

However, studies have shown that the long-term use of marijuana not only destroys nerve cells(Ed. note: I am not aware of any research that even purports to show that marijuana use "destroys nerve cells," and there is substantial evidence to the contrary; however, it apparently has become a part of the party line and to deny it would be pro-drug deviationism.) but causes serious respiratory problems similar to those caused by tobacco use, including chronic bronchitis and lung cancer. (Ed. note: Also, the affects of "long-term use" to "patients with terminal illnesses" would seem to be irrelevant.)

Since there are other, more effective, legal pain-relieving medications available in the market place, I do not support efforts to legalize marijuana, nor do I believe that legalizing marijuana for medical purposes is a viable argument. (Ed. note: If there are "more effective legal medications," why do terminally ill people want to use medical marijuana?) After the passage of a state initiative in California which legalized medicinal use of marijuana, approximately 30 marijuana distributing clubs, or "Pot Cafes"(Ed. note: Does he have Buyers Clubs confused with Amsterdam coffee shops?) opened through out the state. Additionally, since the passage of this state legislation, marijuana use by teenagers in California has doubled.(Ed. note: There is absolutely no data to support this statement. None. Zero. Nada. Zilch. He is lying.
See Medical Marijuana Advocates Accuse California AG Lungren of Lying About Prop. 215 then Lying to Cover-up the Lies )Understanding these statistics,(sic) I cannot, as a United States Senator, support legislation which would undoubtedly bring these same results to our state.

Again, I appreciate your comments in regards to this matter of mutual concern. Please be assured, should this issue come before the full Senate for consideration, I will continue my commitment to ensure that all illicit drugs remain illegal.

Warm regards,

Senator Gordon H. Smith
